ingredients.item: Thinly sliced beef for hot pot (ribeye or sirloin)

instructions: Halve the onion and smash 4 of the garlic cloves. Put the broth, onion, smashed garlic, ginger, wine, bay leaves, star anise, 2 tbsp of the soy sauce and the salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then cover partly and simmer for 30 minutes.
While the broth simmers, soak the vermicelli in warm water for 10 minutes, then drain. Fan the beef out on a plate.

Cut half the napa cabbage into 2-inch pieces and halve the bok choy. Slice the shiitake caps and trim the base off the enoki, then pull the enoki apart. Cut the tofu into 1-inch cubes. Arrange the vegetables, tofu and noodles on plates.

Set out small bowls of the sesame paste, the remaining 4 tbsp soy sauce, sha cha, black vinegar and sesame oil, with the remaining 4 garlic cloves minced, the green onions sliced and the cilantro chopped. Each person mixes their own sauce, for example 1 tbsp sesame paste thinned with 1 tbsp warm water, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1/2 tbsp sha cha, 1/2 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil and 1 clove of garlic, topped with green onion and cilantro.

Strain the broth to take out the onion, garlic, ginger and spices. Set a wide pot of the hot broth on a burner at the table and bring it to a boil. Put the chili oil on the table for the adults to add to their own bowls.

Everyone cooks their own food in the boiling broth. The beef takes 30 seconds to 1 minute, until no longer pink. Enoki take 30 to 45 seconds, shiitake 2 to 3 minutes, and the cabbage, bok choy and tofu 2 to 3 minutes. Cook the vermicelli last, for 2 minutes. If the broth gets low, top it up with boiling water.
Lift each piece out, dip it in your sauce and eat.
method_notes: The lead for the broth is Pups with Chopsticks (5 from 22 ratings): beef broth simmered with garlic, ginger, onion, Shaoxing wine, bay, star anise and soy. The Woks of Life (5 from 17) agrees that the sauce and a pot of hot broth are what matter, and sets out the add-ins and the sesame paste, soy and sha cha sauce. The lead simmers the broth for an hour; here it is 30 minutes using boxed broth to fit a weeknight, and the heat is kept in a chili oil at the table.
